newsitem.title: DUBAI: Shell to list marketing unit on Muscat exchange.
newsitem.headline: Shell to list marketing unit on Muscat exchange.

text.p: Royal Dutch Shell Group plans to divest a 51 percent stake in its wholly owned subsidiary Shell Marketing Oman Ltd in July led by a local stock market floatation, the Omani firm said on Monday.

Forty percent of the marketing firm -- whose main activity is the retail sale of petroleum fuels in the Gulf Arab state -- would be floated on the Muscat Securities Market with a further 11 percent reserved for existing Omani investors.
"We are very close to a final agreement with the government for a floatation in early July," Jack Tabak, administration manager at Shell Marketing Oman told Reuters.
The 40 percent float on the Muscat stock exchange -- which is not open to foreign investors -- would involve the offer of 10 million shares each valued 4.9 Omani rials, Tabak said.
A share offer would close early August allowing shares to begin trading on the Muscat exchange at the end of September.
Shell Marketing Oman Ltd has annual sales of 130 million Omani rials of transport fuels, lubricants and chemicals to the private and government sectors.
It is the largest distributor in the non-OPEC oil state, with 115 retail sites giving it a 60 percent market share.
The Anglo-Dutch oil group would retain a 49 percent stake in the new company which will be formed in September as Shell Marketing Oman Company SAOG as a legally Omani entity.
Its board management would be half Omani and half Shell.
The 11 percent stake would be held by owners of the Oman Lubricants Company, local Shell dealers and employees.
Final go-ahead for the stock market float would occur after Shell received a formal letter from Oman's Ministry of Petroleum and Minerals and its commerce and industry ministry.
The eight-year-old Muscat securities market is capitalised at around $5 billion and climbed 30 percent in 1996.
The float would reduce Shell's corporate tax liability and clear the way for its licences in the company to be renewed.

Shell Marketing Oman currently pays 50 percent corporate tax though this would fall to 7.5 percent once its holding was reduced to 49 percent and the company became fully Omani under local law, Tabak said.
Its operating licence in the country previously came up each ten years because of its status as a foreign registered firm.

The floatation will exclude Shell's upstream and downstream oil and gas assets in the country, including its 34 percent stake in Petroleum Development Oman -- the dominant oil producer in Oman -- and a 30 percent stake in a gas export project. ($1=0.377 Omani rials).
